name: mine_shared
comment: A mine that links the decoder context out of an already finished buffer
(runs/shared_cache) instead of rebuilding it. Those arrays are the loader's own
output, so they do not depend on the policy -- but they are not independent of
the representation either: neighbor time alignment, the geometry correction,
model cardinalities and scene order all have to match the consuming run.
The trainer enforces that by hashing the whole staged model args file on both
sides and refusing anything but a byte-for-byte match. So this arm applies to
re-mining the SAME base -- after a reward change, say, or a resumed order epoch
-- and not to a new base checkpoint, whose args differ in at least its own
bookkeeping even when every shape agrees. There is no partial credit and no way
to narrow the check from a preset: a new base means a cold mine.
Two roots are deliberately left off, because sharing either is undetectable
when it is wrong -- the shapes still agree and nothing downstream complains:
shared_replay_encoding_root is the frozen encoder's OUTPUT. Reusing it across
a different base checkpoint feeds the new decoder the old model's features.
Add it only when the encoder weights are byte-identical, never merely because
the two args.json agree on shapes.
shared_replay_expert_anchor_root links the logged expert arrays, which really
are policy-independent -- but a source mined before the anchor gate existed
has no expert_hard_gate_step.npy, and linking it silently produces a buffer
that expert_anchor_safe_step_scoped cannot use. Recomputing the expert arrays
is cheap next to scoring candidates, so prefer letting the mine write them.
